text:
maria: FYInoticed a regression after the kernel-selector canary change. Small streaming requests see host parse latency ~2.2x and CPU up. Repro + flame below. Looks like tokenization + frame-parse + kvcache churn.

maria: Repro steps (local canary):
```
./harness --mode=stream --seq-len=64 --chunk=64 --concurrency=40 --target=canary-host:8080
```
Observed: parse p50 6.4ms (was 2.8ms), pod CPU +70%.

maria: Sampled pprof breakdown (10s):
- 34% host::parse::tokenize
- 22% host::stream::frame_parse
- 18% kvcache::evict
- 9% grpc::writev
- 7% net::write
pprof: https://perf.internal/pprofiles/1810000123

ryan: :eyes: anything touching key generation or batch heuristics recently? kv evict jumps look bad.

ash: Note: kernel-selector lowered mini_batch_hint on canary to prioritize throughput. Smaller mini-batches -> more flushes could raise small-write overhead.

kai: Checked traces  kvcache miss rate canary ~43% vs prod ~12% on same harness. Keys same logical fields but differing byte order (we started canonicalizing headers in proto->json recently).

lee: If header ordering changed, keys will be semantically equal but byte-diff, causing cold inserts/evictions. Can you paste raw key diffs?

maria: example kv key (hex, shortened):
```
old: 0a2f6b6579..len:72..hash:ab12
new: 0a2f6b6579..len:74..hash:ff3c  # extra 2 bytes due to header order
```

maria: Also noticed grpc frames went from coalesced ~4k -> many 512B frames. Could be reduced batching or proto framing change.

ash: Hypothesis: (A) kernel hint change reduced batch size -> fewer tokens/batch -> more frequent parse/fewer coalesced writes; (B) key normalization added nondeterministic ordering -> high kvcache miss -> evict churn -> CPU spike. Together they amplify.

ryan: Can we toggle kernel selector to legacy to confirm?

maria: With KERNEL_HINT=legacy on same canary build: parse p50 -> 2.9ms, miss rate ~14%. Strong correlation.

kai: Root cause likely twofold as ash outlined. Remedies: revert header reordering in key path OR implement stable key serializer, and set a min_mini_batch in selector to avoid micro-batching regression.

lee: Prioritize kvcache key serializer (lowest blast radius). Also consider gating the selector change behind a flag until telemetry catches up.

maria: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) patch kvcache key serializer to sort headers deterministically, 2) patch kernel-selector to respect min_mini_batch=8. I'll open PRs and run microbench.

perf-bot: perf alert created: perf-1810000123. Baseline p50 parse 2.8ms -> canary 6.4ms. Alert routed to #eng-runtime oncall.

ash: Add a small-chunk streaming microbenchmark to CI (seq len 64) so future changes hit a regression check.

kai: I'll add a telemetry rule to alert if kvcache miss% >20% over 5m post-deploy.

maria: Draft PRs: kernel: https://git.redwood/infer/commit/abf1 (draft), kvcache key: https://git.redwood/infer/commit/cd21 (draft). Will post before/after pprofs once validated.

ryan: When you have pprofs ping me, I'll help validate on canary and run the harness at scale.

lee: :thumbsup: keep the min-batch change short-lived. If key serializer fixes miss rate we can revisit selector tuning.

maria: Follow-up: will post updated pprof + canary numbers here after PR merge. Thanks everyone.
